article.story: CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. -- — Beau Pribula had his best passing game at Virginia, throwing for season-high 294 yards and four touchdowns, as the Cavaliers topped North Carolina 41-24 on Saturday. The win made UVA (6-5, 4-4 ACC) bowl eligible for a second straight year and left Bill Belichick and the Tar Heels still a win shy of that benchmark. The Heels committed two turnovers, missed a field goal and had a second kick blocked. After snapping a three-game losing streak, UVA has now won back-to-back games as it prepares to play at rival Virginia Tech next Saturday. “I honestly do think we’re playing our best ball right now," running back Xavier Brown said. "We really just decided to recommit and finish what we started.” With Carolina playing more 5-man front and man-to-man coverage, UVA shifted to a pass-focused offense, especially finding opportunities throwing to its running backs and tight ends. Of the 19 completions Pribula threw, 13 went to players other than wide receivers. “We had to kind of lead with the pass," UVA coach Tony Elliott said. Pribula connected with receiver Da'Shawn Martin for a 20-yard score in the first quarter, then hooked up with running back Jekail Middlebrook for a 75-yard touchdown play in the second to help UVA take a 20-10 halftime lead. After a strong first half by the offense, Virginia’s defense turned in a pair of key fourth down stops in the third quarter. Pribula found Brown for a 24-yard touchdown with 1:48 left in the period to extend the Cavaliers’ lead to 27-10, and connected with tight end Dakota Twitty for 1-yard score early in the fourth quarter to put the game away. “Not much to say about this one. We couldn’t do anything we needed to do to win. Couldn’t make any plays that we needed to make. And they made a lot of them," Belichick said. "That was just a bad performance all the way around. Out played. Out coached. Out everything.” UNC starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr., who was injured in the Tar Heels' loss to Louisville the weekend before, warmed up but did not play. Instead, the Heels went with freshman Travis Burgess, who entered the game against the Cardinals and threw his first collegiate passes. Burgess finished 25 for 45 for 354 yards, with one touchdown pass and two interceptions. He also rushed for 106 yards and a score for Carolina (5-6, 2-5). “I don't wanna put any pressure on that young man but, man, he's going to be special,” Elliott said. “I think that kid's going to be phenomenal going forward. Because he's got the size, the arm, the athletic ability, but I saw a lot of the ‘it’ factor out of him.” The takeaway North Carolina: The Tar Heels moved the ball behind their backup quarterback, but struggled to score points. UNC racked up 459 total yards. Virginia: The Cavaliers built on the success they found in last weekend's win over Cal and won their second straight game since their open date, notching their most impressive victory since drilling North Carolina State in the season opener. Up next North Carolina: Hosts rival North Carolina State on Saturday. Virginia: Visits rival Virginia Tech on Saturday. ——- Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here.
